dossier.public_summary: The light curve shows odd transits that are about a third the depth of even transits, with a phase curve that looks like a second eclipse of nearly the same depth at half an orbit. Together with wildly inconsistent individual transit depths, this is best explained as an eclipsing stellar binary folded at 13.4 days, not a single transiting planet.

reasons.why: odd and even transits differ at >3 sigma with a large depth ratio; sector_oe_max_sigma 4.988 and sector_oe_same_sign_share 1 show it in both sectors, consistent with an eclipsing binary at half the 13.4 d period (26.8 d) rather than a planet with stable depth.

a second dip of nearly the same depth as the primary (depth_over_dip 0.9357) offset by 0.0602 of an orbit is at the odd/even phase expected for the primary and stronger than any brightening bump, exactly as expected for the secondary eclipse of an EB folded at the half period, not a weak planetary secondary.
reasons.value: snr 4.177, phase 0.5602, depth_ppm 10850, depth_over_dip 0.9357, best_brightening_snr 5.009, secondary_over_bump 0.834

reasons.why: individual transit depths are highly inconsistent, with one transit far shallower than the others that dominate the signal (share_of_top_3 0.984); this supports one population of deep (even) eclipses and a second of shallow (odd) events rather than measurement scatter of a single planet.
